questions.q: What is LoRA's core bet about the weight update needed to adapt a pretrained model?
options: That the update must be full rank to be useful
That the useful update can be well-approximated by the product of two much smaller, low-rank matrices instead of a full-rank matrix
That no weight update is needed at all for fine-tuning
That only bias terms need to be updated
questions.explain: LoRA assumes the task-adaptation update to a weight matrix can be approximated by a low-rank decomposition (B @ A), requiring far fewer trainable parameters than the full matrix.

questions.q: During a LoRA-adapted forward pass, what happens to the original frozen weight matrix `W`?
options: W is deleted and replaced entirely by B @ A
W is used unchanged in the forward computation, summed with the scaled low-rank update; only A and B receive gradients
W is updated using the same gradients as A and B
W is converted to 4-bit precision automatically
questions.explain: The frozen weight W is still used in the forward pass (h = x@W^T + (alpha/r)*x@A^T@B^T), but it never receives gradients -- only the added low-rank matrices A and B are trained.

questions.q: What does increasing the rank `r` in a LoRA configuration do?
options: It decreases the adapter's capacity and reduces parameter count
It increases the adapter's representational capacity, at the cost of more trainable parameters (though still small relative to the full model)
It has no effect on the model at all
It automatically merges the adapter into the base model
questions.explain: Rank r is the bottleneck dimension of the LoRA matrices; a higher r gives the adapter more capacity to represent complex updates but increases the (still comparatively tiny) number of trainable parameters.

questions.q: Which modules does LoRA's original paper find capture most of the useful adaptation signal, making them the most common default `target_modules`?
options: The embedding layer only
The query and value attention projections (q_proj, v_proj)
The final classification head only
The tokenizer's special tokens
questions.explain: The original LoRA paper found that applying low-rank adapters to the query and value projections in attention captured most of the useful adaptation at a good parameter-efficiency trade-off, making them the common default target.

questions.q: What does `merge_and_unload()` do after LoRA training?
options: It discards the trained adapter without saving anything
It computes W_new = W + (alpha/r) * B @ A for each adapted matrix, producing a standalone model with no PEFT wrapper and no runtime adapter overhead
It converts the adapter to a different rank
It retrains the base model from scratch using the adapter as initialization
questions.explain: merge_and_unload() folds the low-rank update directly into the base weights, producing a single regular model checkpoint rather than keeping the base model and adapter as separate pieces.
